title: Chain the calls
description:
Write a class `Calc` whose member functions can be chained:

```cpp
Calc c{};
c.add(5).multiply(3).subtract(1).value();    // 14
```

Each of `add`, `subtract` and `multiply` changes the stored value and then returns **the object itself by reference** (`return *this;`), so the next call lands on the same object. `value()` is `const` and returns the result. A new `Calc` holds 0.
hints: Return type `Calc&`, and end each changing function with `return *this;`: `this` points at the object, `*this` is the object itself.
Start the value at 0 with a default member initializer; `value()` is `const`.
lessonTitle: this, const Member Functions and Chaining
